implementation_notes: Swift replaces the Document/AbstractDocument/trait trio with an attribute: a type marked @dynamicMemberLookup implements subscript(dynamicMember:) and any otherwise-unbound member access becomes a key lookup, so a Document struct wrapping [String: Any] offers car.model without a hand-written accessor per property (SE-0195; SE-0252 adds key-path based lookup with WritableKeyPath). Because each subscript overload has one return type, a document is only as typed as that return type - add typed computed properties or generic helpers for the members that matter. Codable with JSONDecoder is the other realization: the struct declaration is the view and synthesis writes the decoding, at the cost of copying the document.
pitfalls: The subscript can only return one type (often Any? or a JSON enum), so the 'typed' view degenerates into casts at the call site; give the document typed computed properties for the members that matter.
Dynamic member lookup is not a dictionary subscript: car["model"] needs a separate subscript, and a typo such as car.modle is nil rather than an error.
Member lookup prefers declared members and extensions, so a computed property added later shadows what used to be a key lookup - a compatibility trap when the key set is data-driven.

variants.name: Codable structs decoded with JSONDecoder
variants.idiom_name: Codable + JSONDecoder over a JSON document
variants.implementation_notes: Since Swift 4 the view is declared once - struct Car: Codable { let model: String; let price: Int } - and JSONDecoder synthesises init(from:) to turn the loose JSON document into it, so the trait interfaces are replaced by the conformance and the key mapping by CodingKeys or keyDecodingStrategy. Choose it when the document must become typed before use, and the dynamic-lookup form when most of the tree stays untyped and only a few members are read.
variants.code_sketch:
struct Car: Codable { let model: String; let price: Int }   // the typed view
let raw = try JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data) as? [String: Any]

let decoder = JSONDecoder()
decoder.keyDecodingStrategy = .convertFromSnakeCase
let car = try decoder.decode(Car.self, from: data)        // document -> view
let price = (raw?["price"] as? NSNumber)?.intValue      // loose access remains
pitfalls: Synthesized Decodable is all-or-nothing: the first missing or mistyped key throws keyNotFound/typeMismatch and no partial view is produced.
JSONSerialization bridges numbers through NSNumber, making Int/Double/Bool distinctions ambiguous, so routing the document through JSONDecoder is usually safer than hand-casting.
